articles.excerpt: AI coding assistants frequently write SQL or ORM queries that look plausible but fail at runtime because a column was renamed from created_at to createdAt or a field is non-nullable. To prevent schema…
articles.body: AI coding assistants frequently write SQL or ORM queries that look plausible but fail at runtime because a column was renamed from created_at to createdAt or a field is non-nullable. To prevent schema-to-code drift, TokenCap implements schema linking in src/schema/schemaGraph.js . How Schema Intelligence Works DDL Parsing: Scans .sql migrations and Prisma/Drizzle schema files for CREATE TABLE statements, extracting column names, types, primary keys, and foreign keys. GraphQL Schema Parsing: Extracts types, queries, and mutations from .graphql files. Code Entity Linking: Maps extracted schema entities to corresponding backend model classes, Prisma calls, or repository queries.

articles.body: Connecting an application to an Electronic Health Record (EHR) system sounds straightforward. Find the API. Authenticate. Fetch patient records. Send updates. Done. Except healthcare integrations rarely work that way in practice. You might connect successfully but receive incomplete data. A request might time out and create duplicate records when retried. Two systems might use different formats for the same clinical information. Or your application might retrieve patient data without enforcing the right access permissions. These problems often start before the first line of integration code is written. articles.title: Do Less, Do Better: Why Quality Beats Quantity in the Pursuit of Excellence
articles.excerpt: We live in a world that celebrates being busy. The more tasks we complete, projects we start, and goals we chase, the more productive we believe we are. We often measure our progress by how much we do…
articles.body: We live in a world that celebrates being busy. The more tasks we complete, projects we start, and goals we chase, the more productive we believe we are. We often measure our progress by how much we do rather than how much we improve. But what if the real secret to getting better is not doing more work, but minimizing the work we do while maximizing its quality? The idea is simple: Do fewer things, do them exceptionally well, and learn from every result. 1. The Problem With Doing Too Much When you try to do too many things at once, your attention gets divided. You spend your time switching between tasks, learning the basics of different skills, and completing work without giving yourself enough time to master any of it.

articles.title: How "approval phishing" drains wallets without stealing a key (and how to check it in 10 lines)
articles.excerpt: Most people picture a crypto theft as "someone got my seed phrase". A large share of wallet drains we see in scam reports works differently: the victim signs one innocent-looking message, and the atta…
articles.body: Most people picture a crypto theft as "someone got my seed phrase". A large share of wallet drains we see in scam reports works differently: the victim signs one innocent-looking message, and the attacker never touches the key. This post explains the mechanism and shows a short script that checks whether a token approval is unlimited. What an approval is ERC-20 tokens let you give another address (a "spender") the right to move your tokens, up to some amount. Exchanges, DEXs and games use this all the time: You call approve(spender, amount) on the token contract. The spender can later call transferFrom(you, anywhere, amount) without asking you again. The risk: many dapps ask for MaxUint256 (unlimited) so you don't have to approve again.

articles.title: Four years ago, NASA punched an asteroid. Europe's Hera probe arrives this month to inspect the wreckage
articles.excerpt: NASA's DART mission made a cosmic mess four years ago — and now a new spacecraft is ready to scout out exactly what the first-of-its-kind collision accomplished.
articles.body: NASA's DART mission made a cosmic mess four years ago — and now a new spacecraft is ready to scout out exactly what the first-of-its-kind collision accomplished. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft slammed into a small space rock called Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022, in humanity's first test of planetary defense. That's the field dedicated to protecting Earth from the possibility of a calamitous asteroid impact, and DART mimicked how humans could change the orbit of a threatening space rock, taking it off its collision course. The mission definitely succeeded, shortening the little asteroid's orbit around a larger rock called Didymos by about 33 minutes .

It was suggested that these stars could only form from the debris of an explosion 10 times more powerful than the 'average' supernovas . The team behind these new findings suggests that ordinary supernovas could actually account for these stars when the uneven or non-spherical way they fling out matter is considered. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.
